channel.title: Climate Errata: site updates
channel.description: Changes to the Climate Errata website itself

item.title: New page: Papers we checked
item.description: A new page lists every paper taken up in our systematic screening since 22 November 2026, with the outcome, including the many with no error, and a tally for papers supporting and questioning mainstream climate findings. Papers whose possible errors are still with the authors are counted but not named until the authors reply or three weeks pass.

item.title: What we select for review, and where from
item.guid: site:2026-11-22:What we select for review, and where from
item.description: The How it works page now explains how papers, datasets and code are chosen: most-cited recent papers in five major journals, widely cited papers that question mainstream findings (tested the same way), widely used datasets and open-source climate software. Substack, blogs, news, social media and non-peer-reviewed preprints are out of scope.

item.title: Each entry now starts with what the dataset, paper or code is
item.guid: site:2026-11-22:Each entry now starts with what the dataset, paper or code is
item.description: Every entry page now opens with a short "What it is" description of the dataset, paper or software concerned, before the finding, and the register shows the same description on each card. Also fixed: on ten entry pages that link to our Zenodo write-ups, the status label at the top wrongly read "Our write-up on Zenodo (latest version)" instead of the entry's status.

item.title: Fixes we propose; our reports on Zenodo
item.guid: site:2026-11-22:Fixes we propose; our reports on Zenodo
item.description: The How it works page now explains the fixes we send with reports: patches and pull requests for software, affected areas and workarounds for datasets, and corrected analyses for papers. It also lists our two broader reports on Zenodo. The home page mentions the proposed fixes too.

item.title: Entries link to our Zenodo preprints
item.guid: site:2026-11-22:Entries link to our Zenodo preprints
item.description: Entries backed by one of our Zenodo preprints now link to it on the entry page. The links use Zenodo's all-versions DOI, so they always open the latest version. Links were added for the modifiedmk, Ali et al. 2026 and Jin & Pu 2026 entries, and the hourly-precipitation entry now opens version 3 rather than version 2.

item.title: New address: climateerrata.org
item.description: The site now lives at climateerrata.org. The old address, climate-errata.netlify.app, redirects there automatically, so existing links keep working.

item.title: Full write-ups for the High-significance entries
item.guid: site:2026-11-22:Full write-ups for the High-significance entries
item.description: The 11 entries rated High significance now have full write-ups: what was found, with the key numbers, who is affected, the responsible party's response, what users can do, and how to reproduce the result. The other entries will follow.

item.title: Fix details on every fixed entry
item.guid: site:2026-11-22:Fix details on every fixed entry
item.description: Each fixed entry now shows when the fix was made, which version or pull request contains it, which versions are affected, and whether the fix is retroactive. The register separates fixes that are released from fixes merged but not yet released. Release statuses were rechecked on GitHub and CRAN.

item.title: Policies and privacy page
item.description: A new page covers contact first, author responses and disputes, corrections and withdrawals, moderation, a code of conduct, funding and conflicts of interest, use of AI, privacy, and takedown or legal requests. It is linked from the top menu and every page footer.

item.title: Papers that use the affected data
item.guid: site:2026-11-22:Papers that use the affected data
item.description: Entries about a problem in a dataset can now list papers that use the affected data for the affected region and period. The effect on each paper is not assessed. The first lists are on the MERRA-2 Australia and ASOS wind entries.

item.title: Dataset pages
item.description: A new Datasets section has one page for each of 14 widely used datasets (ERA5, MERRA-2, CPC Unified, GPCC, GPCP, IMERG, E-OBS, ICOADS, HadSST4, OISST, IBTrACS, COOP HPD, ASOS, GHCN-CAMS). Each page gives the current version, the producer's known-issues page and contact, our entries, related discussions, a place to ask questions, and an RSS feed. There is also a feed for the whole register.

item.title: Discussion by DOI, site search and a contact form
item.guid: site:2026-11-22:Discussion by DOI, site search and a contact form
item.description: Any paper or dataset can now have a discussion page: enter its DOI on Discuss a DOI. Search covers the register, the datasets and the discussions. Write to us takes questions, private error reports and author responses from people without a GitHub account. A posting policy asks that new error claims go to the responsible party first.

item.title: Climate Errata launched
item.description: The register of errors found in climate papers, datasets and code moved from its earlier home to this site, with 48 entries, filters, a significance rubric and a comment thread on every entry.
